chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) would say:
The basis of a person is his heart, his intellect, his religion, and his chivalry -- that is, whatever he makes of himself. The days change, and all people trace back to Adam equally.

key_terms.أصل: Foundation, root, basis -- the essential nature of something
key_terms.دول: Turns, alternations -- the days rotate fortunes between people
key_terms.مروءة: Chivalry, manliness, moral virtue -- a pre-Islamic Arab concept that Islam elevated to mean noble character

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the true basis and value of a person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Imam Ali (AS) would teach that a person's true worth is defined by their inner qualities -- heart, intellect, religion, and moral character -- rather than by lineage or social status. He further emphasizes that worldly fortunes rotate and that all humanity is equal in descent from Adam, a teaching that would have resonated deeply in the tribal Arab society where lineage and ancestry were the primary markers of status.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
